daily.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
daily.summary: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City have become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.

daily.title: Half of Europe witnessed record heat stress this summer — EU
daily.summary: The EU's climate monitor said this summer was third-warmest for the continent on record. European rivers also registered their lowest average flows since records began in 1992.

daily.title: Expedition hopes to finally solve the Amelia Earhart mystery
daily.summary: Nearly 90 years after Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition to the remote island of Nikumaroro hopes a lagoon anomaly could finally reveal the fate of her missing aircraft.

daily.title: ARD-Deutschlandtrend survey: Germans unite in frustration over the government
daily.summary: On the 36th anniversary of reunification, Germans are dissatisfied with the country's political leaders. They don't believe they'll be able to handle the challenges posed by AI, Russia and Donald Trump.

daily.title: Germany news: Reform row raises fears for Merz's coalition
daily.summary: Germany's conservatives are dialing up the pressure on their center-left partners ahead of crunch talks next week. Meanwhile, Volkswagen's latest cost-cutting push has triggered a furious response. DW has the latest.

daily.title: Ukraine: Kyiv bridges shut after fatal Russian drone assault
daily.summary: The latest Russian attacks killed at least one person and severely disrupted traffic in the Ukrainian capital. Several bridges over the Dnipro River connect western and eastern Kyiv.

daily.title: France: 400 schools closed as student protests continue
daily.summary: Police have made around 2,000 arrests and scores of people have been injured as student protests spread across France. Ministers have called for a "day of dialogue" but students have called for further strike action.

daily.title: Ethiopia: Who could bring the warring sides to the negotiation table?
daily.summary: Ethiopia might be facing its most complex armed conflict in contemporary times. The fragile 2022 peace deal has collapsed. International mediators have failed. How will the country return to normal?

daily.title: Taiwan: first new F-16V fighters arrive amid China threat
daily.summary: The US-made jets, part of an order made in 2019, touched down as concerns grow in Taiwan that support from the United States could be wavering. Washington insists its policy towards Taiwan and China hasn't changed.

daily.title: India news: Delhi protesters turn up heat on election chief, police tightens security
daily.summary: Hundreds have gathered in central Delhi to demand the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, over the deletion of voters from electoral rolls. Follow DW.

daily.title: South Korea demands Ukraine apology over POW disclosure
daily.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's disclosure of the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to Seoul has caused a major diplomatic spat between Seoul and Kyiv.

daily.title: Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
daily.summary: A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

daily.title: Turkey's stock market scandal affects nearly half a million investors. Police have made several arrests and an AKP politician has resigned.
daily.summary: Nearly half a million investors are affected, arrests have been made, and a female politician from the ruling party has resigned. What is behind the stock market manipulation scandal in Turkey?

daily.title: US pressures EU allies to release diesel stockpiles
daily.summary: The Trump administration has urged its European allies, particularly Germany and France, to release strategic diesel reserves to ease fuel prices. The EU was holding an emergency meeting on Friday to discuss the issue.

daily.title: New crew makes the quickest US flight to ISS
daily.summary: The SpaceX spacecraft carrying the Crew-13 team docked with the International Space Station in 7 hours and 55 minutes, setting a new record.

daily.title: EU ministers mull new ways to curb irregular migration
daily.summary: The proposals include setting up so-called return hubs outside the EU and strengthening the border agency Frontex. Greece has even proposed temporarily suspending asylum applications in emergency situations.

daily.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
daily.summary: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.

daily.title: UK police make another arrest in RAF Fairford case
daily.summary: Counter terrorism police said a dual UK-Iranian national was arrested on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts. Five men arrested on Sunday remain on bail.

daily.title: Latvians head to the polls with Russia on their minds
daily.summary: On October 3, Latvians will elect a new parliament with Russia looming large over the campaign. Security fears dominate the agenda, but so does a debate over the economic cost of cutting ties with Moscow.

daily.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever ties amid Tigray fighting
daily.summary: Ethiopia said it was expelling Eritrean diplomats in response to Eritrea's "direct and indirect acts of hostility." Eritrea said it had "no choice but to reciprocate in kind."

weekly.title: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could see drivers pay higher running costs while also increasing carbon emissions.
weekly.summary: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could yet see drivers pay higher running costs while increasing planet-heating emissions.

weekly.title: Germans' biggest fear is the high cost of living, an annual study finds
weekly.summary: What do Germans fear most in 2026? Wars? Global crises? Wrong. Their biggest concern is the cost of living, which keeps rising.

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz lauds NATO with Westphalian Peace Prize
weekly.summary: At a ceremony to honor NATO, the German chancellor warned that Russia will threaten the rest of Europe if it isn't stopped in Ukraine. In other news, the German military will set up its first drone regiment.

weekly.title: France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
weekly.summary: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.

weekly.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
weekly.summary: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers for rejected asylum seekers outside the EU.

weekly.title: Germany debates alleged antisemitism in the Left Party
weekly.summary: The Central Council of Jews in Germany thinks the Left Party is dangerous. Other Jews, however, are showing solidarity with the party. How does that add up?

weekly.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
weekly.summary: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

weekly.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
weekly.summary: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.

weekly.title: Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
weekly.summary: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

weekly.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
weekly.summary: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.

weekly.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding.
weekly.summary: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

weekly.title: Germany news: Volkswagen ends collective wage agreements
weekly.summary: In an effort to cut costs, automaker Volkswagen terminated most of its collective wage agreements in Germany. This could reignite disputes with employee representatives.

weekly.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
weekly.summary: The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.

weekly.title: Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
weekly.summary: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.

weekly.title: South Park satirist pushes for accountability in Cornell gang-rape lawsuit
weekly.summary: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.

weekly.title: UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
weekly.summary: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.

weekly.title: Albania: As corruption cases multiply, experts question whether the anti-corruption drive is addressing the causes or just the symptoms.
weekly.summary: From a former president to the ex-intelligence chief, Albania is prosecuting senior officials at a rate once thought impossible. But do more prosecutions mean less corruption or simply better enforcement?

weekly.title: Global trade weathers Iran, Ukraine and Trump's tariffs
weekly.summary: Over the past six years, COVID, two wars and Donald Trump's tariffs have shaken world trade. With globalization already stalling, is this a temporary shock or the start of a great reversal?

weekly.title: AI: Concern as Germany plans to double data center capacity
weekly.summary: Germany is rewriting the rules to attract data center investment from AI companies. But local communities are becoming increasingly skeptical.

weekly.title: Spain grows fruit and vegetables for Europe, but it's running out of water
weekly.summary: Spain's southern coast produces up to 25% of Europe's fruit and vegetables. But amid intensive farming, climate change and illegal wells, the water it takes to grow them is drying up.

weekly.title: UK: US government questions bail for Fairford base suspects
weekly.summary: The US government sees "the hand of a foreign actor" in the security scare at RAF Fairford, a hub for US heavy bombers in Europe. Donald Trump criticized the suspects being released on bail amid ongoing investigations.

weekly.title: Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
weekly.summary: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

weekly.title: Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
weekly.summary: Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

weekly.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
weekly.summary: Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?

weekly.title: Germany news: COVID vaccine maker BioNTech to close 3 sites
weekly.summary: COVID-19 vaccine maker BioNTech is to close three sites in Germany after efforts to find buyers failed. Meanwhile, Rhine water levels have fallen to record lows after an unusually dry September. DW has more.

weekly.title: Diesel prices are surging putting further pressure on Europe
weekly.summary: Trucks, farms and industry are powered with diesel. Now prices are soaring due to refinery disruptions, supply shortages and geopolitical tensions. A potential US export ban could make Europe's diesel crunch even worse.

weekly.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
weekly.summary: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp faces the first real test of his tenure as coach of Germany's national men's football team. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?

weekly.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
weekly.summary: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.

weekly.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
weekly.summary: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.

weekly.title: European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
weekly.summary: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

weekly.title: Germany news: Are Germans giving up their beloved meat and sausages?
weekly.summary: Germans used to be all about sausages and meat. While those do remain popular, things seem to be slowly changing. There also are new insights into the economic side of East Germany's espionage DW has more.

weekly.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
weekly.summary: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

weekly.title: Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
weekly.summary: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

weekly.title: Russian classroom propaganda glorifies dying for your country, students say
weekly.summary: The Russian government has stepped up its efforts to spread patriotic propaganda in schools. DW spoke to students about textbooks that portray the West as hostile and promote sacrifice for the nation.

weekly.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
weekly.summary: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

weekly.title: 'Lithuanian skies are NATO skies': DW speaks with Lithuanian premier Mindaugas Sinkevicius
weekly.summary: In a DW interview, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius discussed threats to Lithuania from Russia and Belarus, NATO's need for stronger air defense and why military spending alone cannot ensure security.

weekly.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
weekly.summary: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.

developing.title: India news: PM Modi says developing nations unfairly blamed for emissions
developing.summary: PM Narendra Modi has told a climate conference that developed countries emit six times more CO2 than India. Meanwhile, an IIT Bombay professor has been accused of caste abuse. DW has more.

developing.title: Live updates: Trump welcomes Xi to Washington
developing.summary: Donald Trump welcomes Xi Jinping to the US by greeting him personally at the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews. The two are expected to discuss trade, AI, Taiwan and Iran.
